Rashi on Kiddushin 82b:1:1.hebrew: מחטא דתלמיותא - מחט תלמיית — ברושדיי"ר (רקמה) בלע"ז — שהתפירות עשויות תלמים תלמים, שורות שורות, כתלמים של מחרישה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82b:1:1.english: A needle of furrows - A furrow needle — brosder (embroidery) in Old French — for the stitches are made furrow by furrow, row by row, like the furrows of a plow.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82b:2:1.hebrew: שעוברת מן העולם - שבטילה מן העולם. בין שהיא נקיה, בין שהיא מאוסה — יש בה צורך; ואם לא ילמדנה זה, ילמדנה אחר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82b:2:1.english: That disappears from the world - That ceases from the world. Whether it is clean [or] whether it is repulsive, there is a need for it; and if this [person] does not learn it, another will learn it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82b:2:2.english: Fortunate is he who sees his parents - [Both] his parents and his children in a clean trade.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82b:2:3.english: A perfumer - A seller of perfumes.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82b:4:1.english: A deer [working as] a fig dryer - One who dries figs in the field.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82b:4:2.english: A porter - A carrier of burdens.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82b:5:1.hebrew: כל אומניות - אין להן מתן שכר לאחר זמן, אלא שכר המצוי להם בשעתן. אבל תורה, מתן שכרה בא מאליו לאורך ימים; ואף לחולה ולזקן שאינו יכול לעסוק בה עכשיו — אוכל מן הקודמות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82b:5:1.english: All trades - They have no granting of reward at a later time, but only the wage that is available to them at their [own] time. But [as for] Torah, the granting of its reward comes on its own for length of days; and even for a sick person or an elderly person who cannot engage in it now, he eats from [the reward of] earlier [deeds].

Rashi on Kiddushin 82b:5:2.hebrew: שנאמר עוד ינובון בשיבה - יצמחו צמח, ויתייחד שכרן לעת שיבתן — דשנים ורעננים יהיו וגו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 82b:5:2.english: As it is stated: “They shall still bring forth fruit in old age” - They will sprout growth, and their reward will be designated for the time of their old age — “they shall be full of sap and richness,” etc.
